title: Musher Component Document
description: A reusable, versioned definition of one workload — its source, runtime shape, health probes, and configuration contract.
$comment: Structural and type validation only — cross-document reference resolution, slug/directory agreement, and platform capability checks are separate validation layers. See spec.md.

kind.description: Document kind discriminator. Must be COMPONENT.

specVersion.description: Version of the Musher specification this document is written against.

arguments.description: Build arguments keyed by argument name, injected into the image build context (Docker ARG). Build-time configuration only — runtime configuration rides on the workload's envVars.

propertyNames.$comment: spec.md §5.1 / ADR 0007 §4. A build argument becomes an environment variable in the build context, so it takes the environment-variable grammar rather than one of its own.

builderImage.description: Buildpacks builder image. Omitted when not building with buildpacks.

dockerfilePath.description: Path to the Dockerfile relative to the repo root. Omitted when not using a Dockerfile.

strategy.description: How the git source becomes an image: DOCKERFILE or BUILDPACKS.

configKey.description: Key of the organization's saved configuration value. The document holds only the name — the value is resolved elsewhere, when the component is deployed, and never appears in this file. The entry's own key may alias it. See spec.md 5.3.

type.description: Discriminator marking an identity-only configuration reference.

inputs.description: Typed input declarations keyed by input name.

propertyNames.$comment: spec.md §4 / ADR 0007 §4. An input, output and parameter name is lowerCamelCase: it is bound by key across three documents — the input, the connection key that fills it, and the parameter that covers it — and it is read by a person in an install form. Kebab-case survives neither the binding nor a generated SDK type without a translation nobody has to write today.

outputs.description: Typed output declarations keyed by output name.

propertyNames.$comment: spec.md §4 / ADR 0007 §4. An input, output and parameter name is lowerCamelCase: it is bound by key across three documents — the input, the connection key that fills it, and the parameter that covers it — and it is read by a person in an install form. Kebab-case survives neither the binding nor a generated SDK type without a translation nobody has to write today.

ComponentEndpoint.$comment: spec.md §5.2. Every protocol may be PUBLIC. The two published address forms differ — an HTTP-family endpoint publishes a URL, a TCP or UDP endpoint an edge `host:port` address — and that difference is carried by the rules in §5.4 and §6.1 rather than by a constraint here.

containerPort.description: Port the workload listens on inside the container. Below 1024 needs a capability the runtime grants, so spec.md §5.2 discourages it without rejecting it.

protocol.description: Protocol served on the port: HTTP, HTTPS, WS, GRPC, TCP, or UDP.

visibility.description: Reachability: PUBLIC for an externally reachable URL, or PRIVATE for internal-mesh only.

key.description: Name of the environment variable. Uppercase letters, digits, and underscores; must not start with a digit (e.g. DATABASE_URL). Unique within envVars.

value.description: How the value resolves, discriminated on type: LITERAL (the value verbatim, in this document) or CONFIG_REF (a name the document does not hold the value for).

ComponentExternal.$comment: spec.md §5.6. resourceType is REQUIRED for the reason ADR 0018 §5 gives for platformDefault.type — an identifier a document may leave out is one two implementations may read differently, and introducing it later is introducing a required field later. It is ADR 0009 grammar and ADR 0009 registry, read at node scope rather than value scope: a node identity is a different claim from a value compatibility tag, and three tagged outputs do not compose into one.
ComponentExternal.description: A node this platform does not run. It has no image, no compute and no address of its own, and what it publishes comes from the inputs its blueprint supplies. resourceType names what it addresses.

resourceType.$comment: ADR 0009 §1 grammar, read at node scope. The grammar is this contract and the membership is not — an identifier the registry does not name is reserved rather than invalid, which is why ERR_UNKNOWN_RESOURCE_TYPE is capability.
resourceType.description: Namespaced identifier for what this node addresses. The grammar is fixed by spec.md §6.3; the identifiers on offer are published at https://api.musher.dev/v1/reference/resource-types.

name.description: The branch name or commit SHA to build from.

type.description: Which git ref is pinned: BRANCH or COMMIT.

build.description: How the repository is built into an image. Required — a git source has no image until something builds one, and leaving the strategy implicit makes the resulting image depend on the builder rather than on this document.

ref.description: Branch or commit to build from. Omitted when unpinned.

repositoryURL.description: Git repository URL the platform builds into an image.

ComponentHealthProbes.description: Staged health probes: startup, readiness, liveness.

liveness.description: Aliveness gate; failure restarts the container. Optional.

readiness.description: Traffic gate; failure pulls the replica from routing without a restart. Required for a SERVICE exposing a public endpoint.

startup.description: Initialization gate; failure means not-yet-started. Optional.

ref.$comment: Lookahead-free so it compiles under RE2 as well as ECMA-262. The tag colon is the one after the final slash, which is what keeps a registry port (localhost:5000/nginx) from reading as a tag. Only the grammar is here: the floating-tag blocklist stays a semantic rule so it can grow without a major version. See spec.md §5.1.
ref.description: OCI image reference the workload runs from. Must carry a tag or an @sha256 digest — a bare name is an implicit :latest and shifts under the registry.

type.description: Discriminator marking a pre-built OCI image source.

description.$comment: spec.md §6 COMP-DESC-001. REQUIRED, and the component is its only home: a blueprint parameter carries no description of its own and shows this one, so a value is described once, by the document that needs it.
description.description: What the value is and what the component does with it. The install form shows it as the help text of the parameter covering this input.

required.description: True when the component cannot be deployed without a value. A blueprint satisfies a required input by wiring it or by covering it with a parameter, unless its schema declares a default.

schema.description: Data contract of the value: type, format, pattern, enum, default, sensitivity.

target.description: Where the resolved value is bound. Omitted when the consumer injects it manually.

envVarKey.description: Environment variable the resolved value is bound into at runtime materialisation (e.g. ADMIN_EMAIL). Uppercase letters, digits, and underscores; must not start with a digit.

sensitive.description: True when the value is secret material — masked in read surfaces and never echoed back.

type.description: Discriminator marking a verbatim literal value.

value.description: Verbatim value injected into the workload. Empty string is allowed.

ComponentMetadata.description: Identity block of a component document — the name is the file stem.

revision.description: Lineage revision of this component. Required (never defaulted) so the component's content is a pure function of this file, and it is the revision the item's blueprint nodes pin.

allOf.$comment: spec.md §6.2. valueFrom has three members, so the two-branch if/then/else this object carried is no longer total: INPUT would have fallen into the DECLARED branch and been asked for a literal. Each member takes a branch of its own, which is the shape ComponentWorkload uses for type × field validity.

spec.md §6.2. An INPUT output reads a value this component own contract already receives, so `input` names which and `value` has nothing to hold. That the named input exists is not expressible here — the input names are mapping keys elsewhere in the document, which is the line §7 draws for every reference of this shape.

description.$comment: spec.md §6 COMP-DESC-001, for the reason the input carries it.

input.$comment: spec.md §6.2. A sibling mapping key rather than a document reference, so it is spelled as the bare noun a probe and a platform default `endpoint` are and does not take ADR 0007 §1 Ref suffix.
input.description: Name of this component own input the value is read from. Required where valueFrom is INPUT and rejected on every other member.

schema.description: Data contract of the published value: type, format, sensitivity.

value.description: Static value for DECLARED outputs. MUST NOT be present on a DERIVED output, whose value is resolved at runtime.

valueFrom.description: Where the published value comes from: DERIVED from the running workload, DECLARED as a literal in this document, or INPUT read from one of this component own inputs.

endpoint.description: Name of the endpoint whose port the probe targets. Omitted, it selects the primary endpoint spec.md §5.2 elects.

failureThreshold.description: Consecutive failures required to consider the probe failing.

initialDelaySeconds.description: Seconds to wait after start before the first probe.

path.description: HTTP path the platform polls for this probe.

successThreshold.description: Consecutive successes required to consider the probe passing.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for a probe response.

cron.description: Cron expression on which a CRON workload runs.

allOf.$comment: spec.md §5. A component is one of two things, and the key that is present says which: `workload` is a workload this platform runs, `external` is a node it does not. Spelled as an anyOf over `required` rather than as a oneOf so a document naming neither reports ERR_MISSING_FIELD at /spec — the field an author has to add — rather than a branch count; the exclusion below is what makes it exactly one. A spec-level `type` tag was the alternative and would have been a required field on every document ever written, with a oneOf at `spec` putting every default beneath it beyond the effective-value resolution ADR 0008 requires.

spec.md §5.6. Naming both is not a composition: a node this platform does not run has nothing for a workload block to describe. The false schema anchors the diagnostic at the field that should not have been there, which is the shape BlueprintNode already uses for `revision` on a repo-local reference.

spec.md §5.6. An external node exists to publish values another node consumes, so one publishing nothing is a node nothing can need — the argument §5 makes for a SERVICE that exposes no endpoint. An absent contract is a missing field and an empty outputs mapping an invalid value, which is that section two-spelling distinction.
spec.md §5.6. DERIVED means the platform, from the running workload (§6.2), and there is no running workload here. DECLARED and INPUT both stay available.

contract.description: The composition contract: typed inputs the component needs and outputs it publishes.

external.description: What this component addresses when this platform does not run it. Present instead of workload, never beside it.

workload.description: How the component runs: source, runtime shape, endpoints, and configuration.

allOf.$comment: spec.md §6.3. A JSON value's string form is a JSON document, and one value has many spellings — insignificant whitespace, member order, number formatting. `pattern` and `enum` both decide membership on the spelling, so neither can state a rule about the value.

spec.md §6.3. A STRING_LIST's string form is a JSON array, so a `pattern` would decide membership on the array's spelling — the argument the JSON branch above makes, arriving through the member that is a list rather than the member that is a document. `enum` is required rather than merely non-empty when written, because an unconstrained list of strings is what JSON already is and §6.4's derivation would have no members to offer. `format` needs no branch: the one below forbids it wherever `type` is not STRING, and STRING_LIST is not STRING.

spec.md §6.3. Every `format` member names a lexical convention for text, so the field only refines a STRING. `type` is REQUIRED, so this is a `not` inside the `if` rather than an `else`: a document omitting `type` already reports ERR_MISSING_FIELD and should not also collect a format diagnostic.

ComponentValueSchema.description: Data contract of an input or output value (JSON-Schema subset).

default.description: Pre-filled value when none is supplied. Omitted when the value must be provided.

enum.description: Allowed values when the value is a closed enumeration; empty when unconstrained. MUST be empty where the type is JSON, and MUST be non-empty where the type is STRING_LIST, where it constrains each member of the array rather than the array.

format.description: Semantic refinement of a STRING value: EMAIL, URI, ENDPOINT_URL, CONNECTION_STRING, HOSTNAME, or TIMEZONE. Omitted when unrefined, and MUST NOT be present where the type is not STRING. spec.md §6.3 names where each convention is published.

pattern.description: Regular expression the value must match. Omitted when unconstrained, and MUST NOT be present where the type is JSON or STRING_LIST.

resourceType.$comment: spec.md §6.3. ADR 0009 §1: the grammar is fixed here and the membership is not, so this is a pattern rather than an enum, and §6.3 names the surface that publishes the identifiers without restating any of them. Reverse-DNS namespace then one or more lowercase segments, lookahead-free and backreference-free so it compiles under RE2 as well as ECMA-262, which spec.md §11 requires of every pattern this repository publishes.
resourceType.description: Namespaced identifier of the backing resource this value addresses, matched by the blueprint connection gate when wiring the value into a consumer input. Omitted when the value addresses no particular resource. spec.md §6.3 names where the identifiers are published.

sensitive.description: True when the value is secret material: handled as a secret reference, masked in UIs, never echoed back.

type.description: Shape of the value's string form: STRING is any text, NUMBER a JSON number, BOOLEAN true or false, JSON a JSON document of any kind, STRING_LIST a JSON array of strings each drawn from enum.

accessMode.description: How the materialized volume is shared across replicas: READ_WRITE_ONCE (attached block volume, mounts on a single replica) or READ_WRITE_MANY (shared network volume, mounts on every replica).

mountPath.description: Absolute path where the volume is mounted in the workload.

readOnly.description: True when the volume is mounted read-only.

sizeGiB.description: Default provisioned size of the volume in gibibytes.

allOf.$comment: Type × field validity, spec.md §5. Every branch below is a bare conditional carrying no `type`, so lint.ts checkClosedObjects correctly skips it — the object is closed once, by the schema that declares its properties.

spec.md §5. The converse of the branch above: a SERVICE is the kind that serves, so it declares at least one endpoint. An absent block is a missing field and an empty one is an invalid value, which is the same two-spelling distinction the forbidden direction already makes.

spec.md §5.4: readiness is required for a SERVICE exposing at least one PUBLIC endpoint whose protocol is in the HTTP family. Endpoints are a mapping, and no keyword asserts `some member matches` over one, so the condition is spelled as the negation of `every member fails to match`. A PUBLIC TCP or UDP endpoint publishes a host:port address rather than a URL, and an L4 consumer retries where a browser does not, so it compels no probe.

command.description: Command the workload runs. Required for JOB and CRON, which have nothing to run without it. On a SERVICE or WORKER it overrides the image's default command.

endpoints.description: Endpoints the workload exposes, keyed by endpoint name. Only a SERVICE may declare one; on any other kind the mapping must be absent or empty.

propertyNames.$comment: spec.md §5.2. An endpoint name is referenced by probes and by platform defaults, and is composed into a DNS label beside other slugs rather than being one. Alphanumeric keeps any hyphen separator unambiguous; 20 characters leave room in the 63-character label for what it composes with.

envVars.description: Environment variables injected into the running workload. Each entry pairs a key (e.g. DATABASE_URL) with a value discriminated on type: LITERAL (the value verbatim, in this document) or CONFIG_REF (a name the document does not hold the value for). Keys are unique. Build-time values belong in source.build.arguments instead.

health.description: Staged health probes (startup, readiness, liveness). Omitted when none are defined.

schedule.description: Cron schedule a CRON workload runs on. Required for CRON and rejected on every other kind, where a schedule would mean nothing.

source.description: Discriminated image or git source the workload is built or run from.

type.description: Runtime shape: SERVICE (long-running, may expose endpoints), WORKER (long-running, no endpoints), JOB (one-shot command), or CRON (scheduled command).

volumes.description: Default volumes provisioned for deployments, keyed by volume name.

propertyNames.$comment: spec.md §5.5 / ADR 0007 §4. A volume name is materialised as a named volume, so it is a DNS label on the same grammar a node name uses.
